newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-DONG JIONG HAS EASY START AT WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-DONG JIONG HAS EASY START AT WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: China's Dong Jiong, the number one seed and All-England champion, opened his bid to become world badminton champion with a swift 15-6 15-3 win over South Korean Jang Chun-woong on Tuesday.
Jiong, who led his country to victory in the Sudirman Cup team event last week, needed just 25 minutes to claim his place in the last 32 of the world championships.
Ong Ewe Hock, the number six seed from Malaysia, came close to a shock early exit against the tall Ukrainian, Vladislav Druzchenko.
The Commonwealth Games silver medallist had to fight back from 12-7 down in the deciding game before winning 13-18 15-4 15-12.
Earlier in the day, Ye Zhaoying, the women's world number one and All-England champion from China, took just 17 minutes to beat Sandra Dimbour of France 11-4 11-2 in the first round.
She now meets Commonwealth Games champion, Lisa Campbell of Australia, in Tuesday's second round.
Ye's Indonesian rival Susi Susanti claimed a 11-4 11-1 victory over Ng Chin from Hong Kong.
Two women seeds were taken to a third game.

Third seed Mia Audina of Indonesia struggled to overcome Denmark's Mette Pedersen Denmark 11-2 8-11 11-5, while fellow-countrywoman, Cindana, the number 16 seed, came back from dropping the first game to defeat Jeng Schwu-Jen of Taiwan 8-11 11-5 11-2.
